facts.name: Lenten Rose
facts.notes: The first flowers of the year, often open in March, with evergreen leaves. Long-lived and deer resistant.

sources.title: University of Vermont Extension: Growing Hellebores
sources.note: Remove the last of the prior year's leaves in early spring to make room for new growth.

sources.title: UW Botanic Gardens: When and Why to Cut Leaves Off Epimediums and Hellebores
sources.note: Cut epimedium foliage down by flowering time, in late winter.

sources.title: Penn State Extension: Cutting Down Perennials in the Fall
sources.note: Cut peonies, daylilies, brunnera and speedwell in fall; cut bee balm and garden phlox with powdery mildew and destroy the leaves; rake up hosta leaves (slug eggs); cut yarrow and Shasta daisy flower stalks but keep the base leaves. Leave grasses, Siberian iris, baptisia, sedum, Joe-Pye weed, coneflower, black-eyed Susan and most natives standing; leave marginally hardy anise hyssop tops over winter; tidy hardy geraniums, heucheras, hellebores and moss phlox in spring.

companions.why: Combines with barrenwort in spring; later a backdrop for hostas; shown among hardy geranium.
